chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Hafs and one or more of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a man who swears an oath to his brother, saying: 'There is no obligation upon him, for he only intended to honor him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no obligation upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an oath taken to honor someone without intending a binding vow?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the juristic principle of *al-yamin al-mu'arraka* (binding oath) is distinguished from *al-yamin al-lughwiyya* (non-binding, conversational oath) based on the speaker's intent (*niyya*). This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining when *kaffarah* (expiation) is due, emphasizing that mere expressions of respect do not incur the penalty of breaking a vow. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on contextual interpretation (*siyaq*) and the internal state of the individual in legal rulings.
